statement_sources: experiments/EXP-CERTBIN-4e92d7/specification.yaml (object.field, factor_base_subspace, unknowns, curve, summation_polynomial, descended_system, macaulay_matrix, constant_in_row_space)

conventions.field: F_2[t]/(t^17 + t^3 + 1); element = 17-bit integer, bit j = coefficient of t^j
conventions.assignment_encoding: an assignment v is the 18-bit integer with bit i = v_i, so x_1 = v & 511 and x_2 = v >> 9
conventions.monomial_encoding: ascending variable-index list; [] is the constant 1 (as blind-inputs.json)
conventions.Macaulay_rows: (mu, k), mu of degree <= D-2 ordered by (degree, lexicographic index tuple), row index = mu_index*17 + k, zero rows retained
conventions.Macaulay_columns: all multilinear monomials of degree <= D, descending degrevlex, constant last
conventions.W4_dims: dims[i] = dim W^(i) for i = 0..fixpoint_index+1; dims[fixpoint_index+1] == dims[fixpoint_index]

elimination_method: Primary engine (gf2lin.Space): incremental echelon basis over F_2 with Python-int bit vectors, keyed by leading bit; bit b = the monomial of rank b in ASCENDING degrevlex over all multilinear monomials (constant = bit 0), i.e. column c of M_D is bit C_D-1-c and the leading bit is the leading monomial in the spec's descending-degrevlex column order. Echelon (not reduced); rank = basis size; dim(X cap B_{<=d}) = #basis vectors with leading bit < N(d) (valid because the order is degree-graded); 1 in X iff a basis vector has leading bit 0. W_4 by the literal rule (closure.literal_closure): at every iteration the FULL echelon basis of W^(i) cap B_{<=3} (snapshotted at the start of the iteration) is multiplied by every v_j (numpy gather with multilinear reduction) and inserted. Independent cross-check (xcheck.XCheck, no shared code): packed uint64 numpy vectorised Gauss-Jordan to full RREF, own column order (degree descending, reverse combinations order within a degree), rows from the checker's hand-expanded equations; recomputes rank_3, rank_4, 1 in R_3/R_4, dim(R_4 cap B_{<=d}), the W_4 iterate dimensions, fixpoint index, first-one iteration and dim(W_4 cap B_{<=d}). Second cross-check (closure.complement_closure): same engine, different generating set (only vectors independent modulo rowspace(M_3)+previously multiplied); must reproduce every literal iterate dimension. M_5 (Q5): primary engine only.

ambiguities.clause: card Q3 'the list dim W^(0), dim W^(1), ... up to the fixpoint; the fixpoint index'
readings: list also contains dim W^(fix+1), the first repeated value
ambiguities.chosen: the list contains dim W^(0) .. dim W^(fix+1); fixpoint_index = fix = the first i with dim W^(i+1) = dim W^(i), so W_4 = W^(fix)
ambiguities.why: keeps the stopping evidence in the record; either reading is recoverable from the other

ambiguities.clause: e94b27 object.mutant_closure_W_D 'A basis of W^(i) intersected with B_{<=D-1} is the set of RREF rows ... whose leading monomial has degree <= D-1' vs card BR-4 'b in a basis of W^(i) cap B_{<=3}'
ambiguities.chosen: echelon (non-reduced) basis rows with leading monomial of degree <= 3
ambiguities.why: both are bases of the same subspace W^(i) cap B_{<=3} (degree-graded order), so span{v_j b} and hence every W^(i+1) and every recorded quantity are identical; BR-1 allows any correct elimination

ambiguities.clause: card BR-4 'At EVERY iteration multiply a full basis of W^(i) cap B_{<=3}'
readings: basis taken at the start of iteration i
basis updated while products are being inserted
ambiguities.chosen: snapshot at the start of iteration i; products of vectors that enter during iteration i are formed at iteration i+1
ambiguities.why: this is the definition W^(i+1) = W^(i) + span{v_j b : b in a basis of W^(i) cap B_{<=3}}; the fixpoint W_4 is the same either way, the per-iteration dimensions are those of the definition

ambiguities.clause: explicit-kind instances (blind-inputs.json kind 'explicit'); neither specification defines this kind
readings: equations[k] is the set of monomials of f_k, summed over F_2, k = list position
ambiguities.chosen: f_k = sum over F_2 of the monomials listed at position k (k = 0..16), each monomial an ascending variable-index list per blind-inputs 'monomial_encoding'; M_D, W_D and s built from these f_k with the identical conventions
ambiguities.why: the only reading consistent with the file's field names and monomial_encoding; checked: 17 lists per instance, ascending distinct indices in 0..17, no duplicate monomial, max degree 2

ambiguities.clause: card Q3 'the first iteration i with 1 in W^(i), or null'
ambiguities.chosen: counting from W^(0): i = 0 means 1 is already in rowspace(M_4)
ambiguities.why: matches the index of the dims list

ambiguities.clause: 4e92d7 object.constant_in_row_space '1 in R_D iff the constant column (the last one) is a pivot column'
readings: pivot column of the Stage-1 column pass
ambiguities.chosen: 1 in rowspace(M_D), computed as: the echelon basis has a vector with leading monomial 1
ambiguities.why: equivalent: the constant column is last, so it is a pivot column of any column-ordered forward elimination iff some row-space vector has its first nonzero column there, i.e. equals 1 (card BR-1: pivot rule does not affect membership of 1)

ambiguities.clause: card BR-5 validity 'every parent p in products is an EARLIER id'
ambiguities.chosen: earlier in the elements list; ids are 0..n-1 in list order so both readings coincide; the checker enforces list order
ambiguities.why: list order is what a sequential verifier can check

ambiguities.clause: card BR-5 'every g_id has degree <= 4', 'every g_p used as a parent has degree <= 3'
readings: degree of the zero polynomial undefined
ambiguities.chosen: the zero polynomial has degree -1 (passes both bounds); no emitted element is zero

ambiguities.clause: card BR-3 route 2 'count solutions lying in V'
readings: count of x_2 roots summed over x_1 in V
ambiguities.chosen: s = #{(x_1, x_2) in V x V : S_3(x_1, x_2, x_R) = 0} = sum over x_1 in V of the number of roots x_2 in V; compared with route 1 as a set of assignments v = x_1 + 2^9 x_2
ambiguities.why: s is defined as a count of v in F_2^18, and v <-> (x_1, x_2) is a bijection

ambiguities.why: S_3 as written in KN-TECH-b18366 and 4e92d7 object.summation_polynomial; verified against point addition on E_{A,B}
